newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon prime minister asked to form new government.
newsitem.headline: Gabon prime minister asked to form new government.

text.p: President Omar Bongo has asked Paulin Obame Nguema, Gabon's transitional prime minister who offered his government's resignation last week, to form a new government, officials said.

Obame Ngueme offered the resignation on Friday following municipal and legislative elections under a deal to end political strife in the Central African nation. But officials said on Monday he had been asked to form a new administration.

Former education minister Guy Ndzouba Ndama, who served in single party governments in the 1970s and 1980s, was elected chairman of the new national assembly on Monday. He was chairman of Bongo's ruling Democratic Party in the outgoing assembly.
Bongo's party won 100 of parliament's 120 seats in December's legislative election.

That poll, municipal elections in October and elections for a senate or second house last Sunday are part of a democratic timetable brokered in Paris in 1994 to defuse political violence which shook Gabon after Bongo won a disputed 1993 presidential election. Over a dozen people died in the unrest.
Since a 1990 national conference which mapped out Gabon's first democratic transition, the government has included members of the opposition.

Bongo has ruled the former French colony since 1968 after the death of founding head of state, Leon Mba. Gabon, like other African nations, embarked on democratic reforms after the fall of Soviet-bloc communism. Bongo's latest term ends in 1998.
